item.title: The War Room newsletter: Ukraine’s Starlink starvation is a warning
item.description: Satellite communications will underwrite future warfare, writes Alex Turner, our defence editor

item.title: PS Events: Reinventing Europe
item.description: Despite boasting world-leading universities and research institutions, robust trade relationships, a strong industrial base, and a well-established rule of law, Europe has failed to leverage its advantages in a way that would unlock its full economic potential. At the same time, it appears to be punching below its weight internationally, instead of providing the leadership the world so desperately needs to maintain progress toward broadly shared goals.

item.title: A Nobel for the Poor People’s Lawyer
item.description: From growing up in a slum outside Durban to studying law in a segregated university, Navi Pillay’s experience in apartheid-era South Africa instilled in her a lifelong belief in the importance of international courts in defending people’s rights. Now she should use her newly won stature to advance the rule of law at home.

item.title: Does China really prize AI speed over safety?
item.description: In full command of its own cyberspace, China wants the same for AI

item.title: How the Fossil Fuel Industry ‘Captured’ Australia and Maintains Its Political Dominance
item.description: By framing coal and gas as essential to jobs, prosperity and national identity, the industry continues to resist the transition to renewable energy.

item.title: Europe Is Finally Getting Tough on China. Now Comes the Hard Part.
item.description: France and Germany are increasingly willing to flex market share for geopolitical leverage. But they still need reforms to maintain it.

item.title: MAGA at the Acropolis
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s ideologically loaded recent speech in Athens attempted to trace MAGA’s ideological roots back to ancient democracy. But emphasizing the West’s shared civilizational inheritance will not convince Europeans to embrace the hubris of the Trump administration’s imperial worldview.

item.title: Hindutva Goons Unleash Violence on Anti-Modi Protesters
item.description: Activists of the Hindu Raksha Dal, an outfit that furthers the Sangh Parivar’s agenda, were caught on camera beating students and youth participating in the Delhi protests.

item.title: Amid Economic Challenges, China Turns to Vulnerable Workforce to Fix Its Social Security Problems
item.description: China is looking to “optimize and enhance” its social security program. People fear that will translate to pressure on gig economy workers and rural migrant workers.

item.title: Bartleby newsletter: Boomers, babies and bots
item.description: Andrew Palmer, our Bartleby columnist, rounds up three research papers that caught his eye

item.title: A Warm Welcome for US Secretary of State in Central Asia
item.description: Not only can Rubio avoid the most pressing international crises by jetting off to Central Asia, but he – and the Trump administration more broadly – were guaranteed to receive a warm welcome in the region.

item.title: Trump Can Push Past Israeli-Palestinian Paralysis
item.description: Practical steps, U.S. pressure, and greater Arab involvement are needed to overcome trauma and despair.

item.title: What the New China-North Korea Bridge Really Means
item.description: 12 years after construction finished, the New Yalu River Bridge is finally open. Will North Korea's economy open too?

item.title: Breathing New Life Into Organized Labor
item.description: Fulfilling the International Labour Organization’s promise of defending workers’ rights will require more than another declaration or incremental institutional reform. Instead, there must be a concerted global effort to create an enabling environment for all workers and their organizations to operate across borders as easily as capital does.

item.title: Behind the Veil of Religious Harmony in Cambodia
item.description: Aggregate rankings mistake the absence of overt conflict and the fear of speaking up for genuine tolerance.

item.title: South Korea, US Pull Apart as the Alliance Strains
item.description: Restricted intelligence sharing, an investment spat, and remarks by a U.S. commander point to a widening gap between the allies.

item.title: The State That Remembers
item.description: Although many economists believe that AI could drive an economic transformation larger than the Industrial Revolution, and on a vastly shorter timetable, most governments are unequipped to manage such a transition. We urgently need states that can learn on the go and remember what they learn.

item.title: Ecological Imbalance Is Driving Bear Encounters in Mongolia
item.description: As of early October, the Mongolian authorities have received 754 calls reporting bear sightings in various provinces and towns.

item.title: What the Greens Misunderstand About the Ukraine Conflict
item.description: As a policy, the Greens decision to not support military assistance to Ukraine is a deeply flawed one. As a political position it is self-defeating, too.

item.title: China Is a Peer Competitor in a Dangerous Space Race
item.description: Washington needs to take the realities of Chinese advances seriously.

item.title: The End of Abundance
item.description: The decades ahead will be shaped by a contest for natural resources, making the world more prone to stagflation and handing the levers of policy back to governments. Emerging economies that are rich in people but poor in resources will be the most acutely affected but can take practical steps to strengthen their resilience.

item.title: The Iran War Has Changed the World Forever
item.description: Some dramatic long-term consequences are just beginning to come into view.

item.title: Europe’s Credibility Gap
item.description: Ngaire Woods, Dean of Oxford’s Blavatnik School of Government, Class Mertens, also at Oxford, have written a piece arguing that Europe, despite its attempts at self-sufficiency, remains dependent on an unpredictable United States. The continent needs to address this vulnerability so that it can convince other countries, many of which find themselves similarly vulnerable to great-power coercion, that it is a worthy partner.

item.title: A Better “America First”
item.description: Charles Kupchan, who served in the Clinton and Obama administrations, argues that many aspects of Trump's foreign policy are worth keeping and align with changes in the international system. He explains how the next president can marry the good impulses of "America first" with the best of liberal internationalism.

item.title: What Is Behind Bangladesh’s Continuing Law and Order Crisis?
item.description: The government must rebuild public trust in the police force and insulate law enforcement from political influence.

item.title: Pakistan’s Counterterrorism Campaign Is at an Inflection Point
item.description: If the new security framework fails to adopt a holistic approach to counterterrorism, it will once again end up treating the symptoms while ignoring the causes.

item.title: How Congress Fixed Social Security During Its Last Crisis
item.description: In 1983, the realization the program could implode propelled last-ditch compromises.

item.title: After War of Words, China Says Relations With Philippines at ‘Critical Juncture’
item.description: Growing political polarization has the potential to undermine Manila’s ability to handle its ongoing maritime disputes with Beijing.

item.title: Deepavali vs Diwali Sparks New Political Row in Malaysia
item.description: Is the Malaysian Indian Congress using Hindu identity politics to regain its political relevance ahead of the next general election?

item.title: Indonesian Stock Exchange Plunges After Fresh MSCI Downgrade Threat
item.description: Citing the lack of action on promised reforms, the global index provider has proposed demoting the country from "emerging market" to "standalone market" status.

item.title: As America turns against Ukraine, Europe stands alone
item.description: But Europeans cannot fully replace American support, and they face trouble at home
